_about: Source of truth for this file's names, enums and rooms. See chapters/ch2/chapter.json for the full note. Scene order is the enum order: the index in this list is the value Rive stores.

scene.about: Which room the stage shows. Setting the same value again does nothing.

direction.about: forward for Next, back for Back. Set before scene.

scenes.name: loading
scenes.about: The file's default and the Start room before its bird arrives: the empty cream-and-orange room with the standard ball bouncing in the centre. It has no room of its own; the Start room draws it. Not a card; when scene becomes start the ball finishes its bounce, then the bird drops in (no pan, no colour change).

scenes.name: ad
scenes.about: The empty Chapter 1 room: no props, no ball. Ad 1 and Ad 2 play here, and it is the picture File 2 opens on (File 2's from-chapter-1).

tuneLater: **Card 1: the ball's story is this scene's loop** (762 frames, 12.7 s), and the only scene that follows the scene loop guideline so far. It starts the moment the intro ends: the ball slides out of the cuckoo clock's door along the blue perch, bounces on the chair and onto the window, the nine panes flip to tiles and back (the ball is knocked off), and it rolls off the right edge. Once it is out of sight it is removed (put back behind the clock door, also out of sight); 3 s later it slides out again, and the loop repeats. The ball never goes beyond x 1519, so it always leaves with its room. The small loops (their own "Chapter 1 Card 1 Small" layer, which starts when the pan ends) fit the loop with no jump: the minute hand turns twice (24 ticks), the pendulum swings 12 times, the dog's tail wags 3 times, the mouse runs once and waits in its hole, one set of clouds drifts across the whole window (hidden while the panes are tiles), the plant sways and drifts, and the dog's eye follows the mouse (it closes as the mouse approaches, stays closed while the mouse passes, opens once the mouse is past on its way home, and blinks while open). To tune: the shift per contact (the clock, shelf, chair, window, dog bed and floor each have their own), the pause (3.03 s), the eye's timing against the mouse, the dog's tail speed and the clouds' speed.
**Card 1: the dog's eye.** It is asleep while the mouse is in front of it. If it still doesn't read as asleep, the next step is a bigger cue (the head dipping, or a small z).

**Card 2: slide down, climb back up** (finesse round 3, 2026-11-02; loop 450 frames, 7.5 s; the times are Finesse-panel timecodes). Intro: the ball sits on the pink and orange block on top of the stack and rides down with it (squash when it lands, 1.63 s); the pencil tips into place last, 1.95 to 2.25 s with a bounce to 2.6 s; the ball takes a slow look to the left and back until 3.2 s. Loop, the slide: the ball hops off the block at 3.33 s and lands on the purple bar at 3.73 s (the bar dips, the domino wobbles), rolls down it over the right white joint (it squashes), meets the pencil at the bar's low end at 4.03 s (the pencil gives a little), touches the joint's shoulder at 4.23 s, lands on the yellow stick at 4.53 s (it flexes), rolls down it across the slabs to the lower-left joint at 4.87 s (it squashes), slides down TOTAL's left edge from 5.1 s (the card is pressed 4 percent), drops onto the floor at 5.33 s and rolls out to the left, stopping at 5.73 s. Then, on its own, it rolls back right along the floor from 5.83 s, passes behind the C block at 6.6 s (the block gets a nudge) and stops against the pencil's foot at 7.17 s (0.3 s pause). The climb, six small hops every 0.4 s: onto the C block's top (7.9 s, the block dips), the green slab's right end (8.4 s, the slab dips), then three steps up the purple bar (8.83, 9.23 and 9.63 s) and back onto the block (10.2 s, the block dips), then a short settle. Adapted to the art: the bar's high end is under the top block, so the ball lands at x 752; the bar rests on the white joint, so the joint squashes as the ball crosses it and again when it touches its shoulder (in front of the bar's end, for 3 frames); the pencil is the wall that turns the ball back from the bar's low end to the stick; TOTAL's left edge is the only open slide and it ends at the floor on the left, so the roll to the right is the ball's own effort, and the C block stands in front of the ball (it rolls behind it, hidden for about 0.2 s, and the block's nudge is the tap); there is no free spot at the slab ends (the joint and the pencil are against them), so the climb touches down there for 4 frames in front of the joint instead of resting. The ball's highest point is y 394 (388 px on the 375 x 812 phone frame, 137 px below the lowest copy line). To tune: every time above, the hop heights, the pause lengths, how hard each piece reacts.

**Card 3: the #1 mug as home** (finesse round 2, 2026-11-02; loop 432 frames, 7.2 s; the times are Finesse-panel timecodes). The ball rides in hidden inside the mug (a clip hides it below the mug's front rim). Loop: the mug rocks and the ball hops out at 3.77 s, arcs over the left white post and lands on the yellow band at 4.93 s (the band sags and springs it up at 5.1 s), lands on the top edge of the leaning books at 5.93 s (they rock back and settle), hops over the orange book to the shelf's left end at 6.63 s, rolls off it at 6.77 s, drops onto the blue stick's white tip at 7.2 s (the stick flexes), springs down the stick (lands 7.57 s, leaves its low end 8.3 s), taps the FIRST card's top edge at 9.1 s (the card gives a small wobble), falls into the mug at 9.97 s (the mug wobbles on its base) and waits out of sight until it hops out again. Adapted to the art: the leaning books' top is only 18 wide and the orange book beside it is taller, so the ball cannot roll left along the shelf; it hops over the orange book to the left end of the plank and rolls off from there. The blue stick's tip is under the shelf, so the bounce goes right and down the stick (a diving board) and off its low end up to the card. The ball's highest point is y 388 (381 px on the phone frame, 130 px below the lowest copy line). To tune: the times, how hard the band and the books react, the hop heights, the beat the ball waits in the mug.

**Card 4: a streak of hops** (finesse round 2, 2026-11-02; loop 400 frames, 6.7 s; the times are Finesse-panel timecodes). The ball arrives sitting on the crossword flower, carried in by the pan. Loop: it rests there 3.2 to 4.4 s (the stem sways a little under it), then hops flower head to flower head on an even 0.73 s beat (0.67 s in the air, 0.07 s on the flower): crossword flower to the yellow S hexagon (lands 5.07 s), to the purple leaf (5.8 s), home to the crossword flower (6.53 s), and once more round (7.27, 8.0 and 8.73 s), then rests. Each flower dips and tilts as it is landed on and springs back. The hops are as low as the art allows: the hop from the hexagon to the leaf has to clear the crossword head. The ball's highest point is y 439 (432 px on the phone frame, 181 px below the lowest copy line). To tune: one round or two, the beat, the heights, how far each flower dips.

**Card 5: the ball moves between the tile tops while hidden.** Inside the loop the ball goes from one tile top to the next in a single frame (x 877 to 745 at frames 60 to 61, and 617 to 875 at frames 90 to 91) and the wrap now closes: the ball slides from x 875 back to 618 over frames 177 to 179, behind the letter tiles (global pass 3, 2026-11-02; it was a 257-unit jump at the wrap before). All three moves happen with the ball out of sight behind the tiles, so none shows. If the ball should visibly travel between the tops, that is a finesse call.

**Card 1: pieces outside the safe area** (x 560 to 935, y 0 to 812; found in the global pass, nothing moved, a room-by-room call): the Mouse and its Mouse Hole Clip (x 958 to 984, y 697 to 711), the Mouse Hole (x 1069 to 1090, y 692 to 712) and the Outlet (x 930 to 944, y 681 to 703), all past the right line. They are the pieces the ball passes as it rolls off the right edge, which is part of its story.
